CleanupOutcome.description: One artifacts_queue row's fate. ``reason`` is set only on a refusal.
CleanupOutcome.title: CleanupOutcome

CleanupResponse.description:
``POST /cleanup/queue`` and ``POST /cleanup/queue/run``.

The batch endpoint takes a caller-supplied id list and the run endpoint
sweeps every eligible row; both answer the same four counters, and only the
sweep can carry an ``error``.
CleanupResponse.title: CleanupResponse

CompactSilverResponse.description: ``POST /compact/silver/run`` -- enforced, so a failing run is a 500.
CompactSilverResponse.title: CompactSilverResponse

CompactedPartition.description: One partition's compaction, as ``_compact_one`` reports it.
CompactedPartition.title: CompactedPartition

DiskReading.description:
One watchlist target's measurement.

``carried_forward`` marks a reading reused from the previous run because
this one did not schedule it -- which is why ``error`` can be the literal
``"not scheduled this run"`` and mean nothing is wrong.
DiskReading.title: DiskReading

DiskUsageResponse.description:
``POST /disk-usage/run`` -- measures the watchlist, publishes via node-exporter.

``unpublished`` is the *names* of the targets whose measurement was lost,
not a count of them. Worth stating: every other field here is a counter,
and this stage typed it as one on the first pass until the suite said
otherwise.
DiskUsageResponse.title: DiskUsageResponse

ErrorResponse.description:
FastAPI's uniform error body: ``{"detail": "<message>"}``.

Declared once and shared by every route whose refusals carry a string. The
handful whose ``detail`` is a *structured* dict a caller indexes into
declare their own model instead -- those are the ones where the shape is
load-bearing.
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

FlushSilverResponse.description:
``POST /flush/silver/run`` -- enforced, so a failing run is a 500.

``failure_reason`` is not a field here: it only ever rides the 500, inside
``ErrorResponse.detail``. A 200 is a clean run and never carries it.
FlushSilverResponse.title: FlushSilverResponse

FlushStagingResponse.description: ``POST /flush/staging/run`` -- enforced, so a failing run is a 500.
FlushStagingResponse.title: FlushStagingResponse

FreeSpace.description:
``free_space_status()`` -- the floor check every long job runs first.

``free_inodes`` is ``None`` on platforms without ``statvfs``, which is not
hypothetical: this repository is developed on Windows and runs on Linux.
``message`` is set only when the floor is breached.
FreeSpace.title: FreeSpace

HealthResponse.description: ``GET /health`` everywhere: process liveness, never dependency health.
HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse

NotReadyDetail.description:
The body inside a ``/ready`` 503, which is evidence rather than an error.

``ops/coordination_drain.py:_service_jobs`` reads ``active_jobs`` out of
this and counts a 503 as *known positive* evidence -- a draining service
reporting two jobs in flight is answering the question, not failing. The
reason a 503 carries a full body here rather than a message is that the
drain aggregator is fail-closed: an unreadable body becomes ``unknown``,
which blocks a deploy.
NotReadyDetail.title: NotReadyDetail

NotReadyResponse.description:
``/ready``'s 503 as it reaches the wire.

``HTTPException(detail=...)`` nests the payload under ``detail``, which is
why the aggregator unwraps one level before reading the counts. Declared so
the contract says so.
NotReadyResponse.title: NotReadyResponse

PackBronzeResponse.description:
``POST /pack/bronze/run`` -- the 16 keys its opening literal declares.

``mode`` is ``"apply"`` or ``"dry_run"``; this endpoint never deletes a
source object in either.
PackBronzeResponse.title: PackBronzeResponse

Percentiles.description: A latency distribution: ``n`` samples, p50/p95/max in milliseconds.
Percentiles.title: Percentiles

PrunePackedResponse.description:
``POST /pack/bronze/prune`` -- the 26 keys ``_finalize`` guarantees.

The only endpoint on this service that removes bronze data. The bucket is
un-versioned, so a delete is immediate and there is no undo, which is why
the summary reports what survived as well as what went.

Inodes are reported twice on purpose: ``inodes_freed_estimated`` is what
*this run* freed (deleted objects x ~2.24, measured in Plan 131 Stage 0a)
and ``inodes_freed_measured`` is the filesystem delta, which moves with
everything else on the host. A reading, not a proof.
PrunePackedResponse.title: PrunePackedResponse

ReadyResponse.description:
``GET /ready`` for the services whose evidence is ``job_snapshot()``.

``archiver``, ``processing`` and ``dbt_runner`` return exactly this.
``scraper`` returns it with two extra per-surface fields and declares its
own model for that reason.
ReadyResponse.title: ReadyResponse

SnapshotExportResponse.description:
``POST /snapshots/adaptive-refresh/run`` -- ``SnapshotResult.to_dict()``.

**Transcribed from the dataclass, after transcribing it by eye got it
wrong.** The first version of this model listed 19 fields, read off a
truncated grep of ``to_dict``. The dataclass declares 28. The nine missing
ones were the whole caching layer -- ``export_cache_hit``,
``archive_sha256``, ``materialized_snapshot_path`` and the rest -- and
FastAPI would have deleted every one of them from this endpoint's response
in production, silently, with the generated contract agreeing because the
contract is generated from this file.

``tests/plugins/response_model_fidelity.py`` caught it on its first run.
That is the argument for the plugin, written where the next person
tempted to hand-maintain one of these will read it.

The diagnostics and audit fields stay free-form objects on purpose: their
shape belongs to the selector and cohort modules, and a model that guessed
at it here would filter keys out of somebody else's report.
SnapshotExportResponse.title: SnapshotExportResponse

VerifyPackResponse.description:
``POST /pack/bronze/verify`` -- a read-only canary over a packed month.

Deliberately outside the pack and prune single-flight slots: a canary must
stay available while either mutation is running, which is when it is most
useful.
VerifyPackResponse.title: VerifyPackResponse

WrittenPack.description: One pack file, as ``_write_one_pack`` reports it.
WrittenPack.title: WrittenPack

post.description: Delete a caller-supplied list of artifacts_queue rows (status complete/skip).
Sweep all complete/skip rows from artifacts_queue (Airflow DAG trigger).

Compact silver_normalized/observations partitions (Airflow DAG trigger).

**Enforced.** A run failing ``_compact_failure_reason`` returns 500 with
the summary and a ``failure_reason`` as ``detail``; ``compact_silver``
calls ``raise_for_status()``, so the DAG goes red and pages.

Plan 134 Stage C, deploy 1 of 3. First deliberately: this runs daily and
nothing downstream depends on it, which makes it both the smallest blast
radius and the cheapest place for the repaired pager to be wrong. The two
flushes followed on their own deploys, 48 hours apart.

500.description: The run aborted; the summary is the detail.

post.description:
Measure the disk watchlist and publish it via node-exporter (Plan 135 Stage 4).

``include_slow: true`` adds the high-inode volumes (MinIO bronze, Airflow
task logs), which between them take 20+ minutes and belong on the weekly
run only. Everything else is walked on every call and the slow-tier values
are carried forward in between.

Returns **500** when a scheduled measurement failed, so a silently empty
band on the dashboard cannot pass as a successful run.

409.description: Another run of this job is already in flight.

500.description: The run aborted; the summary is the detail.

post.description:
Flush staging.silver_observations to MinIO silver layer (Airflow DAG trigger).

**Enforced.** A run failing ``_flush_silver_failure_reason`` returns 500
with the summary and a ``failure_reason`` as ``detail``; both callers go
through ``sensors.post_json``, which raises ``JsonPostError`` carrying that
body, so the task goes red and ``hourly_analytics_refresh``'s ``notify``
can quote the reason.

Plan 134 Stage C, deploy 3 of 3 — last, deliberately. A red task here skips
the hour's dbt build, as a red staging flush does, but this is the build
that would otherwise have run on stale silver: Stage A's Incident 1 was five
days of exactly that, green every hour.

500.description: The flush failed; the summary is the detail.

post.description:
Flush all staging event tables to MinIO Parquet (Airflow DAG trigger).

**Enforced.** A run failing ``_flush_staging_failure_reason`` returns 500
with the summary and a ``failure_reason`` as ``detail`` naming the tables
that did not land; both callers go through ``sensors.post_json``, which
raises ``JsonPostError`` carrying that body, so the task goes red and
``hourly_analytics_refresh``'s ``notify`` can quote the reason.

Plan 134 Stage C, deploy 2 of 3. Second because the dbt build does not read
staging events, so the hour dbt skips here is an hour it would have built
from unchanged inputs anyway — which is *not* the same as the build being
unaffected: ``flush_staging_events`` sits upstream of ``dbt_build`` in the
DAG, so a red task here skips it. ``/flush/silver/run`` went last, on
deploy 3, because there the skipped build would also have been building on
stale data.

500.description: The flush failed; the summary is the detail.

post.description:
Delete bronze HTML objects that are inside a verified pack (Plan 131 Stage 4).

**Dry-run unless the caller passes ``apply: true``**, and capped by
``max_objects`` / ``max_packs`` in either mode. This is the only endpoint on
this service that removes bronze data; the bucket is un-versioned, so a
delete is immediate and there is no undo.

``year`` and ``month`` are required. Deliberately: the packer can discover
what is eligible because packing is additive, and this cannot, because it
is not.

Returns **500** with the summary as ``detail`` when the run aborted or
refused an object, matching the CLI's exit code — see
``_prune_failure_reason``.

Returns **409** while another prune run is in flight (D3a). Packing is a
separate key, so a pack and a prune may run at once.

400.description: The request arguments are not usable.

409.description: Another run of this job is already in flight.

500.description: The run aborted; the summary is the detail.

post.description:
Pack cold bronze HTML into indexed packs (Plan 131 Stage 2).

Dry-run unless the caller passes ``apply: true``. Stage 2 writes packs
alongside their sources and deletes nothing — deleting packed sources is
Stage 4 and has its own endpoint when it exists.

Returns **500** with the summary as ``detail`` when the run aborted.
``read_failures`` warn and carry — see ``_pack_failure_reason``.

Returns **409** while another pack run is in flight (D3a), which
``sensors.post_json`` turns into a graceful skip.

400.description: The request arguments are not usable.

409.description: Another run of this job is already in flight.

500.description: The run aborted; the summary is the detail.

post.description:
Sample a packed month through the production read path (read-only).

Unlike pack and prune this endpoint is intentionally outside their
single-flight slots and the pack-worker guard. A canary must stay available
while either mutation job is running, which is when it is most useful.

400.description: The request arguments are not usable.

500.description: The run aborted; the summary is the detail.

503.description: A dependency this service needs is not reachable.

post.description: Generate (or dry-run plan) a CI lake snapshot (Plan 120).

400.description: The requested tier is not one this service exports.

409.description: Another run of this job is already in flight.
